title: What the Reformed grant with these Roman doctors
source_text: LXXIII. Etenim Reformati qui Synodum illam probant, cum istis Scholae Romanae Doctoribus fatentur & agnoscunt, illos qui per Dei gratiam convertuntur, conversionis actus libere elicere, & gratiam Divinam praestare quidem infallibiliter ut credant & resipiscant, sed modo tamen qui sit naturae rationali & liberae consentaneus, & sic ut ab iis simpliciter non tollat potestatem aliter agendi, & pios illos actus omittendi.
pass_a_gloss: LXXIII. For the Reformed who approve that Synod, with those Doctors of the Roman School confess & acknowledge, that those who are converted through the grace of God, freely elicit the acts of conversion, & that divine grace indeed brings it about infallibly that they believe & repent, but yet in a manner which is agreeable to a rational & free nature, & such that it does not absolutely take away from them the power of acting otherwise, & of omitting those pious acts.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXXIII. The Reformed who approve that Synod confess and acknowledge, together with these teachers of the Roman school, that those converted by God's grace perform the acts of conversion freely.

They hold that God's grace does make sure, infallibly, that they believe and repent, yet in a way that suits a rational and free nature, one that does not take away from them absolutely the power to act otherwise and to leave those devout acts undone.
